page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores via AWS Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per physical core. For high-speed temporary storage, it bundles 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside a baseline network throughput of 34 Gbps without an integrated GPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-threaded compute and data handling efficiency. The instance achieved top-tier standing in Geekbench single-core (2,381.0) and multi-core (30,301.0) evaluations, alongside strong performance in multi-core stress-ng (128,256.4) and PassMark CPU metrics (60,913.92). In memory-intensive scenarios, PassMark memory performance and cached small-block memory bandwidth (9,194.14 GB/sec) scored in the top decile. In application-level benchmarks, the instance recorded top-tier results in software compilation with Clang (103,819.0), Redis SET throughput (181.85 million operations per second), PassMark database operations (59,174.39), and static web serving (177.9 GB/sec).

Qualitatively, the ARM-based Graviton architecture paired with dedicated hardware threads delivers high computational density and predictable per-core execution. The bundled 3,800 GB NVMe SSD storage reduces latency and eliminates external network block storage overhead for scratch or caching tasks. However, workloads requiring specialized x86 vector extensions (AVX/AMX) or dedicated hardware accelerators are constrained, as CPU-based LLM inference metrics register in the median tier. The instance is optimally configured for high-concurrency microservices, large-scale software compilation, in-memory caching layers, and high-throughput transactional database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance driven by 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz. Designed without simultaneous multithreading, it allocates a dedicated physical core per vCPU alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The configuration integrates 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 34 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, Clang compilation throughput, and database transaction capacity, reaching 181.85 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking x86 vector instruction sets and accelerator hardware for heavy machine learning inference, its high core count, dedicated physical execution, and substantial direct-attached NVMe storage deliver strong resource density for caching layers, multi-threaded CI/CD pipelines, high-traffic web serving, and distributed database workloads.
